searchText: Congrats on 60M gaslimit everyone What's next you think? 90 mgas blocks and then decreasing slot time to 6s which together would be an effective tripling? the slot time decrease has been consistently presented as being gas limit-independent, i.e not a backdoor way of doubling gas limits it's a big enough change on its own this is not a comment either way on gas limit increases per se It gets you to the same place either way (assuming clients would be able to handle a gas doubling when SSS goes in). Though, that brings up a bigger point. If the slot time is now a variable which may change in future hard forks, we should stop discussing the gas limit as amount of gas per slot but instead as gas per unit of time (mgas/s). Slot time changes should *always* come with a compensatory gas limit change. We should not be trying to sneak in gas limit increases by adjusting the slot time (same for increasing slot time, gas limit should increase). Ideally, client configs would specify "gas per second" rather than "gas per block". the latter part is an important point. But yeah, at least each of the gas limit increases so far has had to content with specific blockers (the 36M -> 45M one had to wait for pectra, etc), and specific risks (contracts found which unintentionally used mispriced opcodes), or were feasible within a fork but prompted specific benchmarking and performance improvements (going to 60M). These are substantial efforts both in terms of individual clients and ecosystem coordination entirely aside from a slot time decrease so tying the two together is a good way of stalling one or both i.e. ending up in a situation where, ok, the slot time decrease can work, but people aren't sure about a sudden doubling of the gas limit, so neither happens You make a good point that gas limit increases should be separately implemented from slot time changes. Ethereum roadmap trends in the direction of making block building more expensive. Do you agree that we should only move away from local block building if clients keep a reliable local-builder fallback? Please react 👍 / 👎. Local building as requisite
